text:
alex: Hey team — hitting a nasty one running the Python SDK async client inside our FastAPI app. Intermittent RuntimeError: 'There is no current event loop' and sometimes the whole worker stalls (high latency).

alex: Minimal repro: using sdk.AsyncClient() in a dependency, requests start fine but after a token refresh/ retry backoff the app becomes unresponsive for a few seconds.

alex: Code:```py
# FastAPI dependency
from redwood_sdk import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(token=... )

async def get_client():
    return client

@app.get('/ping')
async def ping(client=Depends(get_client)):
    return await client.generate('hi')
```

alex: Observed stack: the token refresher calls a retry/backoff routine that uses time.sleep and sync requests in some code path. When that happens uvicorn worker latencies spike and tests fail with 'RuntimeError: cannot schedule new futures after shutdown' in CI. :grimacing:

maria: @alex had a similar one last month — it looked like the auth refresh (inside SDK) fell back to a sync code path when httpx.AsyncClient raised certain errors. The sync fallback uses requests + time.sleep.

maria: Quick workaround: create the AsyncClient per request? or make the refresh outside request path so it doesn't block. But both are meh.

sam: Repro'd locally. Also saw warnings about "asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop" in pytest-asyncio tests where tests call sdk.sync_helper() which did an asyncio.run internally.

sam: Root causes I see:
- SDK auth/refresh logic not fully async (has sync fallback paths)
- Backoff uses time.sleep in those sync paths
- Some public helpers call asyncio.run() for convenience which breaks in event-loop contexts (uvicorn, pytest-asyncio)

jules: Thanks for the report. This looks high priority — blocking production latency. Can you open a minimal repro repo? If not, I'll PR a quick patch: replace blocking sleeps with asyncio.sleep in async code paths, avoid asyncio.run in helpers (provide coroutine alternative).

alex: I can make a tiny repro tonight. The flaky CI failure is the blocker.

maria: Note on typing: the AsyncClient stub doesn't have the same TypedDict/overload signatures as sync client which made it hard to spot we're hitting sync code path. A fix should include improved type-level separation so mypy catches misuse.

sam: Workaround we used: run SDK sync client inside a ThreadPoolExecutor for refresh paths (ugly), or ensure token refresh happens at startup outside request handling. Both reduce incidents but not ideal.

jules: Plan: I'll open an internal bug and attach to eng-runtime. Proposed changes: (1) audit auth/refresh to be fully async with httpx AsyncClient only, (2) replace time.sleep with asyncio.sleep or use anyio, (3) remove asyncio.run in helpers and add async context manager (AsyncClient.__aenter__/__aexit__), (4) add typing overloads for AsyncClient to mirror sync API, (5) add e2e test under uvicorn/pytest-asyncio.

jules: Also adding a deprecation note: if users pass sync-only transport, warn during init instead of silently falling back.

ci-bot: Created issue RED-4123: "async client blocking backoff & sync fallback causing event-loop errors" and linked workspace: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-4123 :white_check_mark:

alex: Awesome — thanks @jules. If you want, I can attach the failing CI logs and my local repro.

maria: small nit: consider exposing a `sync_fallback=False` flag so libs that really need sync fallback (scripts) can enable it explicitly, while servers keep strict async-only flows.

jules: Good call. Adding that to the PR notes.

sam: For immediate mitigation, adding a middleware that catches long sync-blocking calls and logs stack traces was handy for us. Saved a couple of hours chasing this. :pray:

alex: I'll upload the repro shortly. Thanks all.
